papers.title: 3D Printed Polymeric Hydrogels for Nerve Regeneration.
papers.abstract: The human nervous system lacks an inherent ability to regenerate its components upon damage or diseased conditions. During the last decade, this has motivated the development of a number of strategies for nerve regeneration. However, most of those approaches have not been used in clinical applications till today. For instance, although biomaterial-based scaffolds have been extensively used for nerve reparation, the lack of more customized structures have hampered their use in vivo. This highlight focuses mainly on how 3D bioprinting technology, using polymeric hydrogels as bio-inks, can be used for the development of new nerve guidance channels or devices for peripheral nerve cell regeneration. In this concise contribution, some of the most recent and representative examples are highlighted to discuss the challenges involved in various aspects of 3D bioprinting for nerve cell regeneration, specifically when using polymeric hydrogels.

summary_en.motivation: The lack of inherent regeneration in the nervous system motivates the development of new strategies for nerve repair.
summary_en.method: This review highlights recent advances in 3D bioprinting of polymeric hydrogels as bio-inks for nerve guidance channels.
summary_en.result: Customized scaffold structures are identified as a key challenge for in vivo nerve regeneration.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation is presented; the paper is a literature review.
